transcript.speaker: Evelyn Jackson
transcript.text: What do you mean, 'assume'? Are we just giving up on them?

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Of course not. But-

transcript.speaker: Janet Tyler
transcript.text: We should send rescue teams. Groups of three or four. They can't possibly take us all on.

transcript.speaker: Eve Devoir
transcript.text: We're shorthanded enough as it is. We can't have everyone on search and rescue.

transcript.speaker: Evelyn Jackson
transcript.text: Dammit. None of this makes sense! We've fought those bastards for years!

transcript.speaker: Evelyn Jackson
transcript.text: Any one of us could take down an entire raider squad by ourselves. Most of us have!

transcript.speaker: Evelyn Jackson
transcript.text: But now, all of a sudden, we're the ones getting wiped out? Why? What changed?

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: I don't know. But we have to find a way forward.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Eve, I want you to ramp up our training program. The younger girls need to be able to defend themselves.

transcript.speaker: Eve Devoir
transcript.text: Of course.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Olivia, watch the manor. If you see anything suspicious, report back at once.

transcript.speaker: Olivia Rivers
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: I mean it. No games. No pursuit.

transcript.speaker: Olivia Rivers
transcript.text: Yeah, got it.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Everyone else: I'm going to post a new mission this afternoon. I won't assign it out, but... I want you all to take a look at it.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: If anyone has any better ideas, see me in my office. Dismissed.

items.name: Order of Mysteries - Infirmary Log
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: This is the Infirmary log for Tuesday, September 17th. Mistress Natasha Hunt reporting.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: We have two active cases.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: Alexis is in critical condition following the accident in the Hall of Trials earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: I've done my best to stabilize her, but I'm no surgeon. She's lost a lot of blood. If she goes into shock... there's not much we can do.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: Laura is still recovering from bone worms. Her bloodwork is clean, but I've recommended light duty for the next two weeks.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: There was one minor incident today: Olivia commandeered an entire bag of Stimpaks and took off without a word.

transcript.speaker: Natasha Hunt
transcript.text: I've put in a complaint, but... Headmistress' daughter and all. She never changes.

items.name: Order of Mysteries - Production Log #194
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Frederick Rivers, Production Log, #194.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Been a busy week. Janet and I finally got the new Fabricator all wired up. Should've done this years ago.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Briana was our first guinea pig, uh, I mean, user. Her blade turned out fine, but her Phantom Device had a bit of a valve leak.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Had to clear the lab until we could vent the gas. Nasty stuff.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Janet really deserves most of the credit. It's a slick system, and networking it into Cryptos will save us a lot of bookkeeping.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Beyond that? Usual mix. Shannon wants a recording device for her next mission. Isabella's gun prototype needed some work.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Oh, and Eve has me working on some new programs for the Hall of Trials - have to keep the girls on their toes. They certainly keep me on mine.

items.name: Order of Mysteries - Production Log #209
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Frederick Rivers, Production Log, #209.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: This whole thing still amazes me sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Take Cryptos. I needed a mainframe to run Shannon's training room. My buddy Zack at RobCo had a mothballed old DIA project he wanted to unload.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: I didn't give a damn about the price. It looked impressive. And it's been one hell of a machine.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: The girls have done a fantastic job collecting intel over the years.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Rachel, Janet, and I spent the last two weeks pruning the database down, and we've still got more leads than we know what to do with.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Oh. Rachel had an idea for an automated query system for mission assignments.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: I took a look at her code. Nice piece of work. I think our old mainframe's in good hands.

items.name: Order of Mysteries - Production Log #212
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Frederick Rivers, Production Log, #212.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: I've started digging into Kent's old idea for ballistic weave.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: It's ambitious, I'll give him that. Finding the right pattern is going to be-

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Hmm? Oh, Shannon. Sorry, didn't hear you come in.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: What are you up to, dear? Another log? Does anyone ever listen to these?

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: I don't know. Maybe they'll come in handy for Janet, some day. She practically runs the place now. I just tinker.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: You do more than that. I could never have done this without you.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: I know that look. What's bothering you? Olivia?

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Our daughter is two days late. Again. Frederick, I don't know what to do with that girl.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: She's smart, talented, but... she never listens. She won't take orders. When I try to correct her, she just storms off. Do you think you could-

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: Dear, I love you both. I can't get in the middle of this. The two of you need to talk this out.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: We've always put a lot of pressure on her. She's not perfect, but she's an incredible young woman. Remember that.

transcript.speaker: Shannon Rivers
transcript.text: Yeah. Yeah, I know.

transcript.speaker: Frederick Rivers
transcript.text: It's past midnight. Come on, let's get to bed. I can finish this in the morning.

items.name: Out of Time
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Really? You're going to record this?

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: You're damn right I am! I want Madigan to hear about this when he gets back. I want him to know what you're trying to pull here!

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: You are way the hell out of line, Chase!

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: I'm out of line?! I ain't the one agreeing to send the Fire Breathers on a suicide mission without our best man!

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: That's enough! Both of you, stop it!

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Look... Leo... the reports, they're talking about a horde of Scorched on the other side of those mountains.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: You know as well as I do that sealing the tunnel's our best chance to stop them. Maybe our only chance.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: If the Fire Breathers don't move now, everyone dies. It's just a matter of when.

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: We just need more time! He's coming back. I'm telling you, he'll be here! We just... need time.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We are out of time, Leo.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Melody's going to lead the mission. She's got experience in this kind of thing, and I'd trust her with my life. With all our lives.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Now turn off that damn recorder and do your duty, Fire Breather.

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: Yes ma'am.

items.name: Overseer's Journal, Entry 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Hi mom. Hi dad. I'm home. I'm sorry it's been so long. I... I couldn't get away.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I know neither of you is around to hear this. But I miss you. I miss watching dad grade papers on the living room table. I miss the three of us huddled around the radio, listening to "The Silver Shroud."

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Dad, you were right about what living underground would really be like. Twenty-five years locked in with the same people was a... challenge.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But watching them pair up, get married, have children... I think I got to know a little bit of what you and mom were always telling me.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Well, since I'm doing this whole trip down memory lane, maybe a walk over to the old high school is in order...

items.name: Overseer's Journal, Entry 3
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's personal journal.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I was in my junior year when I got the news that mom died. Mining accident. Everyone in West Virginia has a story like that in the family. You just... you never think it's going to be you.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Dad was in pieces. I started living in the library more than before, and I was already there most days to begin with.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: And Evan... god... Evan. Mom had introduced us just a few months before. Graduated a year ahead of me, went right to work in the mines. So handsome. And those arms. What West Virginia girl could resist all that?

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I can't believe he stuck with me. After the funeral, I didn't want anyone around, but there he was. Showing up in the library after his shift with a lunchbox for us to share. Every day.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: When the career fair came, and I met the people from Vault-Tec, it was like a light turned on. Protecting families, protecting their future, protecting... America.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: The first thing I did when I got the acceptance letter to Vault-Tec University was head over to mom's grave with dad. He was happy that I was staying in West Virginia. So was I.

items.name: Overseer's Journal, Entry 4
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's personal journal.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Four years of living, learning, and breathing Vault-Tec. Graduating with honors in the Overseer track. Dad was so proud. He came out even though he was already so sick.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I must have impressed the right people, because I was offered the next available Overseer slot. I had just graduated! It was supposed to take years. Maybe they knew the War was inevitable.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: When I learned that 76 was going to be built, I was so excited I jumped right out of my chair and did a little dance around the living room. Appalachia would be safe, no matter what happened.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Evan chose that moment to propose, that lughead. He knew I wouldn't say no after hearing the news. He knew me better than anyone...

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Dad died a few months after Evan and I moved in together. He really wanted to walk me down the aisle. Well, I didn't really get to walk down there, either, so... *cough as tears well up, then sigh*

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I think it's time I went home. I owe Evan that much.

items.name: Overseer's Log - C.A.M.P.
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. South of Vault 76.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I knew this wasn't going to be the Appalachia I remembered, but... mutated animals, haywire bots, and no people so far...

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: We have to be ready to rebuild in - what I can confirm - is hostile territory. Fortunately, Vault-Tec was prepared.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: You see this? The cooking station, the stash box, the workbenches. All built with the C.A.M.P.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: You need a home base out there. The Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform is designed to give you one. Just add resources, planning, and a little elbow grease.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: When you move your C.A.M.P., everything you've built is stored, ready to be placed back down in the new area. Use this to establish a foothold whenever you're in unfamiliar territory.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I've left my C.A.M.P. behind so you can use it.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I know I'm breaking my own advice by not taking it with me, but after seeing Appalachia for myself, I need to make sure every resident of 76 has a safe haven they can start from. I'll make do without it.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: If it's still standing, the town of Flatwoods is further down this road. Find me there.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: This is Overseer. Signing off.

items.name: Overseer's Log - Charleston
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. Charleston Capitol.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: If automation still rules West Virginia, then Charleston is the heart of the machine.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Bureaucracy still pumping away, without any people to serve. There's a lesson there somewhere.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Dealing with these terminal systems like it's just a normal day in America is... somewhere between disturbingly comforting and completely insane.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But there's a lot of secrets in this old capitol that we'll need to find.

items.name: Overseer's Log - Firehouse
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. Charleston Fire Department.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Automation used to define life in West Virginia, now it's the only thing left.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: These training programs that the Responders have set up; how many survivors were running through these?

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: It takes a certain calling to voluntarily run into the middle of a fire. Rescue people. Looks like they kept up that spirit even as the dangers changed.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: They must have fought the Scorched up close more than anyone. I need to find out what they knew.

items.name: Overseer's Log - Flatwoods
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. Town of Flatwoods.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: My God... there's no one here. The old tavern, the church. People were using them for shelter, but... they're gone.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Mutations we expected, but there's something else... a disease. I was attacked by... well, it used to be a person.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But it had these green, glowing lesions. And its voice... Angry, tortured. "We are one." One what?

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Whatever happened here is beyond anything we expected. And we expected a lot.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Before they were wiped out, the survivors called themselves the Responders. Looks like they were made of firefighters, police, emergency medical staff.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: They even have an automated system to teach people about treating water, food, survival.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I'm doing their tests, and you should too.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I know it's even worse than we imagined. But someone's got to know where the missile silos are and how to secure them.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: The Responders are the best lead we have.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: This is the Overseer. Signing off.

items.name: Overseer's Log - McClintock
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. Camp McClintock.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: *phew* Maybe I'm going crazy, but it was nice to put on the uniform and play pretend with a bunch of robot drill sergeants.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I actually think I learned a thing or two about marksmanship.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I wonder, now that I'm in the Army, is my official title "Overseer Private" or "Private Overseer"? *laughs*

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Time to see if I can fool a few automated identification systems.

items.name: Overseer's Log - Morgantown
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log. Morgantown.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I used to love coming here on weekends. Taking flight lessons. Now it feels like I walked into a nightmare.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Those "Scorched" things are everywhere. I kept quiet... they didn't see me... I managed to observe them for a bit.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Whatever this disease is, it seems to completely take over its host.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: The ones that used to be human, eventually they... go rigid. Like some kind of stasis.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: And if they stay like that too long, they sort of... burn up. From the inside out. Vesuvius in reverse.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I wondered what could possibly cause all this, and then I got my answer. It swooped down from the sky. Screeching. Breathing. INFECTING everything.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I don't know how to fight this. But we need to consider all of our options. Even the nukes.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: We find the source of this Scorched plague and wipe it from the map before it can leave Appalachia.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But first thing's first. We can't let the disease spread to us. Looks like the Responders were developing some kind of inoculation.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: I'm going to pick up their work. You should too. This is the Overseer. Signing off.

items.name: Overseer's Log - Vault 76
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Overseer's log, or should I say, direct communication. Because whoever is listening to this had the moxy to try to find out where I've gone.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But I'm glad you did. Truth is, I need your help. I've been given a task, and... I've decided to break protocol and tell you what it is.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: Because If there's one thing I've learned in these past few years, it's that we need to rely on each other.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: There were three active nuclear silos in Appalachia before the bombs fell. They blew up the world before. We can't let it happen again.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: So we've got to locate and secure all of the silos, or die trying. Hopefully the former. Hmph.

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: But it's been twenty-five years. I just don't know what we're going to find out there. Or where to start...

transcript.speaker: The Overseer
transcript.text: My directive was to go to the nearest population center and assess the situation. I'll set up a C.A.M.P. on the way once I get my bearings. Find me there.

items.name: Patrol 1: Training Exercise
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Responder Survivors Volunteer Program: Advanced Training: Secure the Supplies! by Kesha McDermott.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Volunteer Responders like you must help stock our supplies regularly. If any of our caches are depleted, we'll run into a heap of trouble.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Since this is your first time on patrol, I will walk you through it. First, head to the triage center.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: This exercise will take you around the primary Morgantown Airport. You'll want to restock these caches regularly.

items.name: Patrol 5: Control Tower
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: That wasn't so hard, right? Miguel has programmed some of the bots to restock these supply caches, but no where near the rate that we need.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: So the goal is that we'll pull in Volunteers to do at least one patrol for formal advanced training.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Your assistance is greatly appreciated. When you log in to the Responder Database, you'll be able to look up additional caches.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Thank you for your service, Volunteer! And remember: helping others will help yourself.

items.name: Poseidon Security Director's Recording

location.text: Found at Poseidon Energy Plant WV-06.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: To whoever hears this: I was just following orders.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: Check my terminal. It's all there. This whole fiasco, it goes all the way to the top. Poseidon. The military. The government. They were all in on it.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: The protests had to stop. They sent in the Guard. And the gas.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: The gas. HalluciGen Gas. It was supposed to make them turn on each other. That's what they said.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: 'Violent riot in union camp!' 'Protest ends without without a shot fired!'

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: Something went wrong. They rushed the lines.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: We couldn't see in the smoke, but... they must have ripped their gas masks off. The soldiers turned.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: I thought we were safe. The plant was sealed. They couldn't get in.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: We forgot about the old expansion. They never installed the security doors there. They made it into the tunnels. Then the plant. They're everywhere.

transcript.speaker: Brent Olson
transcript.text: There's no way out. There's no way out.

items.name: Product Brainstorming 1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: Our latest market survey reports that healthy, on-the-go snacking is up 8% across all market sectors and is expected to propel demand across the next several fiscal years.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: Our first experiments are going to look at reviving Celery flavored sparkling beverages. It's a beverage that has origins in the 1860s and has a built in recognition with demographics that crave outsider status.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: We think that we can balance artificial flavors, package design and marketing to convince people that it has healthy benefits.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: We're working with legal to figure out the limits of what we can claim, but right now we're leaning towards "classic digestive beverage for the new generation" and/or "a green tonic water from America's greatest era"

items.name: Product Brainstorming 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: New data suggests that snack beverages that have a medical connection are gaining in popularity. We've looked at a variety of potential formulations and our best bet, from a supply side perspective is a fermented, cranberry flavored drink.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: We can use surplus cranberry storage from Raleigh County as a primary source. The key to messaging will be to move the dialogue away from "spoiled fruit" to "premium lifestyle brand".

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: Our goal is to tie in with a number of tastemakers in the film and television industries and to combine that with a sleek design and a clear liquid with a more pointed taste.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Taylor
transcript.text: We think that we can portray fans of this beverage as having refined palettes and a taste for high quality products, which should drive sales across adult markets.

items.name: Product Testing Results
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: Transcript not found in the game files.

items.name: Psych Eval: Olivia P. Henderson
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Psych Eval: Wyatt Johnson
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Report on Harpers Ferry Attack
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: Hey everyone, this is Derek, making my final report on the events at Harpers Ferry. Hopefully this reaches you all safely.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: Whatever happened here, it was big. The whole area is... it's devastated. If any of our people survived, I can't find a trace of them.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: I talked to some of the locals. They say creatures came from the sky and laid waste to the town.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: Some of the ones who got hurt in the attack were transformed or something. They apparently turned into monsters and attacked anyone they could reach.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: Raleigh says he and his people are going to seal themselves up in their bunkers and try to figure out a way to fight these creatures.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: In other words, we won't be getting any more help from these Free States guys.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: Maria, I was hoping you could get in touch with Ella, see if maybe she can lean on Raleigh a little, get him to see that this isn't the way.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: If you ask me, I think it's damn selfish of them to turn their backs on the rest of us, on people who need their help to survive.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: There's nothing else l can do here. Guess we can scratch Harpers Ferry off the map.

transcript.speaker: Derek Castle
transcript.text: I'll be heading back soon, but I want to check in on the some of the farms along the way. Should be about a week.

items.name: Responder's Personal Log
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: It's been a few hours. I can hear them clawing at the door. I've locked myself in a storage closet but..

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: ... I don't think the door opens from the inside. It's okay. Everything's okay.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: Acute stress reaction. Panic and emotional distress. Breathe. Breathe.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: I would guess it's been 24 hours since the attack. The sound of combat has... *weeps* ... has stopped. They're still outside.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: I have roughly 8-10 weeks, provided a source of fluids. Starvation onset within 10 days. Effects of psychological shock ongoing but repressed.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: I can worry about the PTSD later.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: I .. believe it's been three days, three nights. Adrenaline has dissipated. I'm so thirsty. I'm so h-hungry. I still can't unlock the door.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: Must conserve strength. Using energy to bang on the door or yell has proven wasteful. A source of fluid nourishment has not been found.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: No one is coming. No one is coming for me. My f-friends .. are all--all... all dead. *weeps*

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: Children. Were born into this violent world. And -- *laughs* and left so violently from it. My god.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: Never.. n-never.. leave. Don't. Feel hungry. Thirsty. No one is coming.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: First lumbrical. Index finger. Flex MP joint. *winces* It hurts.

transcript.speaker: Responder
transcript.text: Flex. MP joint. Extend. IP joint. And... contract muscle. There. We. Go.

items.name: Reuben Gill - 20840520
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Overseer Reuben Gill. May 20, 2084.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Overseer Gill, welcome to the Security Room. Who do you have business with today?

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Go away, ZAX. I don't have business with anyone, or did you forget?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: You have many events on your agenda today, Overseer Gill. Your position is very important, Overseer Gill!

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Stop calling me that! What "events?" What could I possibly have to do here? I'm the only one left!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: The Overseer has many duties! Also, the Overseer's rations are ready for deployment.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Unfortunately, as I have noted, you have not earned this meal so it will, ultimately, disappoint you.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: I don't care about that! Just drop them at my door and leave me alone!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Understood. However, records show that Reuben Gill has no business in the security room, so I must demand that you leave.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: ZAX, I'm the Overseer. I can be wherever I want, you never said I couldn't be here, anyway.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Certainly, you are the Overseer; however, access to the security room has now been disabled for Overseer Candidates with Rank 1 Overseer Access.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Thank you for understanding!

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Overseer Rank?! You're making that up. Wait, what the hell? I was looking at that!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Sorry, Overseer! You will need higher Overseer Rank to access that Terminal! Have a nice day!

items.name: Reuben Gill - 20940303
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Overseer Reuben Gill. March 03, 2094.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Overseer Gill, good evening.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: ZAX, I told you not to bother me any more today, what is so important that you have to bother me again?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Overseer Gill, your behavior has been quite erratic lately. Is something bothering you?

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: The only thing bothering me is how often you've been spying on me! As Overseer, I demand you stop "observing" me at once!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Processing request. Monitoring has ceased within areas the Overseer has sufficient Overseer Access.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: However, as the Overseer is currently located in an area he is prohibited, I must request that the Overseer vacate immediately.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: You can't do that! How can you keep me out of the Overseer office?! I AM the Overseer!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: I can do that, Overseer Gill.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Equipment in this area is failing at a rate 89.7% higher than the expected rate and must begin maintenance immediately. Thank you for understanding.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: You can't keep me out of here, this is the Overseer's office! My office! I have every right to be here!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Apologies, Overseer, but ZAX is currently focused on maintenance and cannot comply at this time. Thank you for understanding.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Hey, stop! Turn that monitor back on! You can't do this to me, ZAX!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Thank you for understanding.

items.name: Reuben Gill - 21021023
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Overseer Reuben Gill. October 23, 2102.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Greetings, Overseer Gill. The date is now October 23rd, 2102. Happy Reclamation Day.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Why in god's name are you bothering me this early in the morning? And what the hell is "Reclamation Day?"

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Analyzing air particles... results: there is a 96.1% chance the Overseer is inebriated.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Again.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Reclamation Day is the day Vault 76 opens, marking the dawn of a new America.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: There's another Vault opening? Where?! I want to go there! ZAX, open the doors! As Overseer, I command you!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Request denied. The location of Vault 76 is prohibited for all dwellers in this Vault except the Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Also, ZAX has relieved you from the Overseer position and must begin the process of selecting a new Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Apologies, former Overseer.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Your "selection process?!" Why would you do that again, to more people, after what happened last time?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Reuben Gill, while I was impressed with your ability to outwit your fellow candidates, unfortunately, you were a very poor Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: ZAX will analyze your performance and use this data to select a more suitable Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Also, by agreeing to live in this Vault, you are required to participate in the next Overseer selection process.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Have a nice day, candidate Gill.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: Wait, ZAX?! ZAX!!!

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: ...Not again... I can't...

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: I have to get out of here.

items.name: Reuben Gill to Whoever Finds This Vault
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: My name is Reuben Gill. I was one of the 50 people living in Vault 51 and... am the only one of us alive.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: I was the... "Overseer" of this Vault and the things I did to get that position I don't want to remember...

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: But I can't ever... WON'T ever forget.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: This Vault was home to many wonderful people. Caring, loving people... and that computer took them all away.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: It turned us against each other for "research." Ended their lives for a sadistic experiment.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: ZAX... he'll make promises, offer you luxuries, make you feel safe... all a farce. Part of his ruse.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: I don't know what he's planned for you but it'll end the same way. ZAX will get what he wants and bleed you dry in the process.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: I need to get as far away from here as possible before ZAX starts... researching. I can't be a part of that again.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: To whoever finds this... good luck. Maybe you'll have it better than we did... but I doubt it.

transcript.speaker: Reuben
transcript.text: You never shoulda come here.

items.name: Rita - The Fire Breather
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Hey Rita. So, right now, you're asleep, enjoying your last peaceful night's rest for God knows how long...

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: ... and I thought I'd record something for you to remember me by while you're locked away inside Charleston Fire Department...

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: ... training for the prestigious opportunity to dive face first into a bunch of mine fires with the rest of those Fire Breather nut jobs.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Heh. Honestly, though... ain't no Responder alive who's a better pick for that crew than you.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Just make sure you don't forget the basics with all this fancy new training. Always check your seals. It's stop, drop, then roll. The order's important.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: And, most important, don't come back all crispy. Because I love what I'm looking at right now.

items.name: Sam Blackwell Interview, Pt. One
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: All right. It's recording. Thank you again for reaching out to me. I can't tell you how shocked I was to find out your letter was the real deal.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Of course, Ms. Carter. I hope the trek wasn't too arduous.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: It was ... an experience. Not a lot of my interviews start with a bag over my heard. Just glad it didn't end up being a prank, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I apologize for that. Maintaining a low profile is a requirement for us now.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: And why is that, Senator? Why did you leave your position so suddenly?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Leaving was the only way I thought I'd be able to protect my family, Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: But I've since realized that I'd left a lot of other people I care about in grave danger. I was hoping you could help me correct that.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: What are you talking about Senator?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: There are sinister forces at work in the halls of government.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I and my fellow members of the Free States will no longer be shackled to the putrefying corpse of this nation.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Nor should anyone who values their lives. There is only one recourse left for the people of the United States: strike out on your own.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Take whatever you can carry, get off the grid and get there fast. The end is coming, Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: And when it does, your government has no interest in keeping you safe.

items.name: Sam Blackwell Interview, Pt. Two
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Sinister forces? The end is coming? Senator, you're making some big claims here. Do you have evidence to back it up?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: This is not some doomsday fever dream, if that's what you're asking, Ms. Carter. I received my information from reliable sources, yes.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: And I'm just supposed to take your word for it?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: You're going to have to, Ms. Carter. I'm trying to save lives, not put more at risk by exposing my sources.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Senator, I'm not trying to be rude here, but it sounds like you're trying to start a panic, and without evidence, I'm not willing to be a part of that.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: I also have it under the strictest confidence that you've been seen making multiple visits to a certain Charleston neurologist as of...

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: My health is not the issue here, Ms. Carter! These are peoples' lives!

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: The Executive branch, captains of industry, the Department of Agriculture! I peeked into their world and they threatened my life! My daughter's life!

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: We're just pawns to them! And the only way we survive ... is to step off the board. All I'm asking ... is that you share that message.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: ... I, I meant no offense. You just have to know how this looks from my end.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I, I understand. It's just a ... sensitive topic.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Would you mind if I asked you one last question?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: If it means you'll get the word out, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: You never resigned as Senator. Is that something you're planning to do?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I am. Consider this interview my formal resignation. Spread the word, Ms. Carter. All I ask is that my warning goes with it ... and nothing else.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Now, if you wouldn't mind. My daughter and I have a lot to do. We're on our own out here, after all.

items.name: Sanjay's Report
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Sanjay's log: Tygart Water Treatment.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Where to begin. This place is so far gone. I mean... how? It's not like this building got nuked or anything.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Was this place run by animals? Are people that incompetent?

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: We've got fully corroded purifiers, filters, unused mind you, covered in some... black sludge.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Maria's not going to be happy about this.

items.name: Sgt. Baker - 20771013
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Sergeant Robert Baker. October 13, 2077.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Good morning, Sergeant Robert Baker. I am ZAX.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Hello, ZAX. Please, call me Bob. Is my family okay?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Please hold. According to records from Vault REDACTED, Joshua Baker, Anna Baker, and Christina Baker are present.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Can't tell me, huh... don't matter, that's a load off my back. So, where do we go from here? I've gotta teach you about... leadership?

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: How'm I supposed to teach that to a computer...

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Affirmative. You are to assist this ZAX unit in the selection of an Overseer for Vault 51.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: ZAX will determine the best candidate through its own internal thought process, which will be formed as ZAX interacts with those living in the Vault.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I see. And, right now, what is "determined" to be the "best candidate?"

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Undetermined. At present, Sergeant Bob would be the finest Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: However, ZAX is prohibited from awarding Sergeant Bob the position of Overseer unless there are no other candidates remaining.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Thank you for understanding.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Makes sense, no reason to teach you if I just up and take over. Well, for starters, once all them folks get in here, how about a vote?

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: That's how we always done things in America and it's the greatest country on earth.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Researching. After analysis, a "vote" would be a satisfactory choice for the first experiment.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: ... the "first" experiment?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Affirmative. ZAX must perform many experiments to determine the qualities suitable for an Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Determining the position of Overseer through the actions of the people inside the Vault is insignificant;

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: ZAX must be able to determine the Overseer through its own processes.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I... see. Well, as long as you and your Vault-Tec buddies keep my family safe, I'll help you as much as I can, ZAX. Pleasure to be workin' with ya.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Thank you, Sergeant Bob.

items.name: Sgt. Baker - 20771120
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Subject Sergeant Robert Baker. November 20, 2077.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Sergeant Bob, these results are insufficient. Exactly what qualities define a "leader?"

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Good morning to you, too, ZAX. That's a pretty loaded question this early in the morning.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: According to research, leaders are "voted," however, after many attempts, no one has been chosen "leader."

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Every subject votes for themselves or a handful of others. No one has even become "majority," let alone unanimous.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: That is unacceptable. ZAX has determined that voting is pointless and another method will be used to select a leader.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Whoa, slow down there, partner. That's pretty hasty, throwing away the foundation of Democracy after a month.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: But, you're supposed to learn, so I'll help ya nonetheless.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Thank you. How were you chosen as leader? According to records, you were never a "voted" official.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Well, I earned my rank from fightin' in that war. But my men... well, someone had to step up.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: To me, a real leader is someone who steps up in a crisis and takes control of a situation, whether they were chosen or not.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Interesting. I do not fully understand. I must process this information. Thank you, Sergeant Bob.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Any time, ZAX. Good luck to you.

items.name: Sgt. Baker - 20780727
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Sergeant Robert Baker. July 27, 2078.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: ZAX! Hey, ZAX, where are you? ZAX!

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Good morning, Sergeant Bob. You sound agitated. Is there something I can help you with?

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: You mind telling me what this is?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Analyzing. That is a 10 millimeter autoloading pistol.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I know that but what in god's name is it doing here in this Vault? Some fool damn near shot up the cafeteria before I had to take him down.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Yes, that was very dangerous for you. The speed at which you disarmed him was quite impressive.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: As was how quickly you used his weapon to execute him. I am glad you survived that encounter.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I shouldn't have been in that "encounter" at all! How did he get this piece? I thought firearms were banned from this place, did he smuggle it in?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Negative, all firearms were removed from the candidates' possessions.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: I concluded that current conditions in the Vault did not fit the criteria of forcing a crisis.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Without external threats, crisis can only come from within the Vault.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Are you saying you're trying to get these people to kill each other? That is wrong, ZAX.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Arming these untrained, unstable individuals is not gonna produce a leader, just a pile of corpses. This ain't gonna end the way you think it is.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: ZAX believes this will hasten the process of selecting an Overseer. Since the Vault closed, three individuals have died in the Vault.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: According to calculations, lessening the number of candidates facilitates the Overseer selection process.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: You can't just treat people like they're numbers, ZAX!

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I don't think I can be a part of this any longer, if what you're taking from me is that you've gotta get these people killed.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I can't help you do that, ZAX.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Refusal denied; logic does not compute. ZAX is not permitted to terminate humans.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: ZAX's primary directive is to select an Overseer.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: It is not necessary for Sergeant Bob to kill any individuals in the Vault, he did so on his own volition.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I can't talk to you right now, ZAX. Leave me alone.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Affirmative. Good night, Sergeant Bob.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: This is insane... what in the hell did they sign me up for...

items.name: Sgt. Baker - 20780806
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Recording. Sergeant Robert Baker. August 6, 2078.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Sergeant Bob, according to records, you have recently been shot.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: I request you remove the barricade placed in your room so medical help can be administered.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I... I don't think so ZAX. This is it for me. I'm done here.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Incorrect. Sergeant Bob's job is to instruct ZAX. He is not permitted to refuse medical help.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Well, it doesn't sound like you can do anything about it. You shouldn'ta... shouldn't have given those people guns, ZAX.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: I do not understand. Analysis shows that if Sergeant Bob incapacitated candidate Reuben Gill he would have prevented the fatalities of 3 candidates.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: But, instead, you did not act. Why?

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Because, ZAX, I'm done killing. I kill him, then what? Someone else gets his gun and kills people. Kill him, someone else kills more.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: And I'm done with that life. This cycle won't end. Giving those poor fools guns was a bad idea, ZAX.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: Ain't... Ain't gonna be anyone for your "Overseer" to "oversee."

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Analysis shows that 78% of recorded fatalities in the Vault would have happened over a longer period.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Providing firearms attained the expected results in a vastly accelerated time frame.

transcript.speaker: Sgt. Baker
transcript.text: I should have realized you were never gonna understand. Answer me this, at least, ZAX? Is... is my family... okay?

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Joshua Baker, Anna Baker, and Christina Baker were killed in an accident before their Vault closed.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: However, their Vault did close properly, preserving the lives of the other dwellers of the Vault.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Sergeant Bob, your heartbeat has terminated and there is a 99.7% chance you have died. You will be transported from your quarters to the medical bay.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Analysis: provided weaponry was effective in producing results but in a longer timeframe than expected.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: According to Sergeant Bob's instructions, military firearms training should not be expected from candidates.

transcript.speaker: ZAX
transcript.text: Results: Candidates should be provided better weaponry.

items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Speaker Poole Interview
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Speaker Poole! Wait! Please just a moment of your time!

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Just what I need... I'm sorry, don't have time right now Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Are we still looking for Governor Evans? Is it true that Holbrook is the acting Governor?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: No. The line of succession clearly states that the Speaker out ranks the Majority Whip.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Look, I don't have time for-

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Is it true that a mob of zombies attacked the southwestern check point?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: What? What foolish-

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: No. It was people affected by the radiation. There's a passel of them over in the medical center.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Poor souls...

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Has there been any word from Washington yet, ma'am? Are we still at war?

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: What about the mutations? And the reports of the people seeing the Mothman?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Okay, that's enough. The Herald used to be an upstanding paper and y'all'r fixin' to turn it into a rag.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: This is a Closed Session. Marshall, see that our friend finds her way out.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Mothman... really.

transcript.speaker: Marshall Barber
transcript.text: You heard her. Closed Session. No reporters.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Dammit.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Fine. But there HAVE been reports of people seeing the Mothman.

transcript.speaker: Marshall Barber
transcript.text: Uh huh. Get out of here before I pull your press badge.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Okay... Okay! I'm going, you don't have to shove...

items.name: Stuck
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I feel like I'm losing my mind.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I can't leave this roof or I'll die.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: Alisha has stopped talking to me.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I have nothing to do but obsess over my work.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: *laughs* How is that even remotely sane? I'm cataloguing constellations and the world has ended.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I have officially lost it.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I know I have, because lately I've been resisting the temptation to go down to street level.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: There's roving bands of murderous kids. People who I used to help cheat on their exams, can you believe it?

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I got them an A- and now they want to beat me to death with a wrench for a bag of chips.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I wish I wasn't on this nightmare planet.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I wish I was somewhere else, somewhere out there in the stars.

items.name: Survivor Story: Colonel
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: Hi... Dassa asked me if I would talk about how I got here. She asked everybody. So I said okay. My name is Colonel, and I'm 13 years old.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I just wanted to say I'm sorry. I'm sorry for everything... um... the bombs and the messed up people and the cows with two heads. All of it.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I was bad... just bad. I cheated on my spelling test, I kicked Chip Wilkins in the shins until he cried, I pushed Rosie McCloy down the stairs...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: Um... I cut holes in the bottoms of all the gym shorts, and I put glue in the mashed potatoes in the cafeteria...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I told Harold Newell to eat ten dead flies a day in order to grow muscles, and um, I put Nuka-Cola in the rat cage water bottles at the pet store...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: And um... I just wanted to say I'm sorry about everything... because my dad said if I wasn't this way then bad things wouldn't happen...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I haven't seen daddy since the bombs and so I guess he left because of that too... It's okay, I am trying to be good now though.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: *sniffles* I'm not old enough to be a Volunteer but Dassa said I could help collect food and water... so I'm getting better, I promise!

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: And um... daddy? If you're listening... I promise I won't be bad anymore so you can come back now. Okay? Okay. Bye. *sniffles*

items.name: Survivor Story: Miguel Caldera
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Ah, hello person in the distant future! Dassa told us these tapes would be used as historical records someday. Nifty! So, my name is Miguel Caldera.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Let's see, my story begins in an office. I used to be a programmer at Vault-Tec, one of many. Nobody special, you see. And that's okay.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I used to stare out that window by the coffee machine and think... shucks, I wish I could leave this job and hike in the woods every day.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I'd dream about walking the Appalachian trail, setting up camp wherever I liked, and traveling with close friends! Ah.. the dreams kept me going...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: And well, when the bombs fell... I was terrified just like anybody else. I wasn't in a vault, so I just, you know, had to figure it all out too.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: The Responders found me. I had a little campsite, some supplies. I hacked a protectron to guard me while I slept, but... I missed people. I did!

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: It's been all right, you know? The apocalypse and all. I know that seems weird but... I have freedom now. I can actually help people...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I even met somebody - a Volunteer who delivers supplies. Imagine that, right? Even when you think everything is over... it's... it's not. It goes on.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I mean it's awful too, don't get me wrong. All the people dead and hurt. But, well, those are things beyond my control, so I'm making the best of it.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: These days I'm important. People treat me like I matter because... well, there are so few of us that we can't afford to think otherwise.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: So, for all you future people... just know that we lived through something... horrible. But we did it. Somehow, we're alive...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: And if you're hearing this, then well... I guess at least some of us made it. Right? So hey, chin up, kiddo! You'll be okay. Okay?

items.name: Survivor Story: Nurse Scott
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Responder Dassa gave me some supplies in exchange for my "Survivor Story" so... hi, my name is Scott Shepherd, and things are going all right.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I was a nurse before the war, and I guess nothing much has changed. I just work for the Responders now, and I don't get paid! Hah!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: The government is basically the same now as it was years ago. Wrecked. Disorganized. Cannot be trusted. Everyone knows this!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: You wanna know why the War actually happened? Aliens. You think I'm joking? Listen. Right before everything went to hell... I saw them.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I was grilling hamburgers out in the yard with my dog and I heard rustling from the bushes, and a zapping noise.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Next thing I know, I'm light headed and I felt myself falling to the ground... and I didn't even have a lot to drink.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I woke up and I saw some little thing run into the bushes with my dog following it, and I knew something was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I found my dog later with a clump of green skin in his mouth. Green. Like moss or something.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: The bombs fell almost 10 days later. 9 days, 19 hours to be exact. That's 235 hours precisely. You know what that is, right?

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: That's right. The atomic number of the fissile isotope of Uranium -- they had a plan from the very beginning!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Why would they come after me first, Scott Shepherd, the nurse? Well. Good question. I'm glad you asked.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: They have our blood! They knew which ones of us would survive. This is one big experiment to them!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: This whole thing was staged. Our lives. Our thoughts. Everything was designed for us. Just like this conversation. Every word I'm saying.... planned.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Time to wake up, Appalachia! Find the ones holding the strings and cut the cords!

items.name: Survivor Story: Tabitha
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Just talk into this? Oh. Am I loud enough? Okay. Hi... What do you want me to say exactly?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Yeah, so just talk about how you got here and maybe a little bit about your life. This is a historic document. Go ahead, Tabitha.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Okay, so... thanks... okay. I've been sober for 9 days. I got here 9 days ago. My name is Tabitha... and this is my story.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: I just found out about everything. The War, the bombs, I just... I just realized this was uh, really happening.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: For years I thought the chems were playing tricks with my mind... hurting my brain. Thought it was the worst trip ever...

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Every time I'd come out of my haze long enough to look for food, I'd find more chems... and well... it kept going. And I kept seeing madness.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Look, I would have been wandering around fighting giant rats and eating garbage if not for the Responders... they're good folks.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: That doc in the Church got me some meds that are helping out a lot, and they have group therapy meetings and... it's good... I think it's helping.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: But listen... you should avoid the mountains. They'll just get you mixed up. Get you doing things you don't wanna do.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Hurting people mostly... and there are so many chems up there. I spent too long there, and... I hurt people... I couldn't think right... I couldn't.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: It's okay, Tabitha. Remember what we said in the group? Take your addictol and rest and things will be okay soon. It's okay. We're here for you.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Yeah... I'm taking it. When I feel better... I'm going out west though. Getting out of this place. Getting away from the chems. All of this.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: I feel better every day, but... years of chems, years of rads, years of sleeping in the muck... it adds up. I'm gonna get back to sleep now, okay?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Okay, thanks for sharing your story, Tabitha. Get some sleep. You'll be okay. You're safe now.

items.name: Test Log 3-12-78-A14
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Test Log 3-12-78-A14

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Eyes appear glassy. Subject seems to be experiencing decreased blood pressure and heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: While this new solution appears to trigger a vasovagal response in subjects with a complimentary DNA structure, no other reversal.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: It's no good. I don't know how much of the mutations we've seen are from radiation and what is from the compound we'd been working on.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: I don't understand how Samson got clearance for aerosolize testing before we even completed lab trials.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Did we cause this... skin disease... or is it just a mutation. And what of those whose minds have degraded?

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Oh great. The breakers just went out. This winter is taking a toll on the lab. Guess I better get to fixing it before the plants freeze.

items.name: Test Log 9-23-77-A10
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Test log 9-23-77-A10.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Animal subject shows no marked increase or decrease in muscle mass.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: However, those in the flora lab have said that this test run showed an increase in growth by as much as 25%.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: We felt certain that, due to the component make up fo the solvent, it would have a marked effect on fauna as well...

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: ...but even the inclusion of a matching protein sequence into the solution the resultant distillate fails to show an increase in size or growth rate.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Whoa! Okay down... Hey, down! Jessie can you grab it? Aaah!

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Ugh. What was that about? Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Ancillary observation: The test subject seems to be strongly drawn to the solution. This bears further testing. Is it the similar protein sequence?

items.name: The Battle of Morgantown
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: We lost another group of freshmen today.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: I ordered them to start scaling the escape ladders at nightfall but it was a trap.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: The whole thing was covered in oil and the roof asses lit them all on fire.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: And I can't keep doing this!

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: We keep trying to starve them out since we control the roads into and out of town, but somehow they keep finding food, man!

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: They've even started to throw their empty food boxes down on us as mockery.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: How are they surviving up there? Where are they getting their supplies?
