items.name: The Big Day
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Wait, is that... you brought a holotape recorder?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Oh, um... yeah. There's something I wanted to document. Don't worry, it's nothing weird, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Anyway, you asked where I like to go to be alone and think, and here we are.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: When I was a student at VTU, I always thought Summersville was one of the prettiest towns I'd ever seen. It was... quaint, you know? Old-fashioned.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Now it's lost all of its charm for me. I just see a sad, decaying place filled with the ghosts of a forgotten world.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: What draws you here? Is it the silence?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: The view, actually. You can see the floodlands perfectly from here.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: The mud flats? Why? There's nothing to see there. It's a ruin.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Because I never want to forget how lucky I am to be alive.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I volunteered for the mission to Pleasant Valley because I was bored and wanted some excitement in my life. I know, I was young and stupid.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: We weren't even an hour outside the city when we heard the blast from the dam. We looked on as the river washed half of Charleston away.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I lost every friend I had on that day, and for a long time, I felt like it was unfair that I survived. Like I should have died with them.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: But that all changed on the day I met you, Amy. You gave me a reason to want to be alive.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: That's why I wanted to ask you...

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Jeff, don't. I know what you want to say, but... now isn't the time. I don't know if it ever will be. I just can't think about that right now.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: It's not that I don't care about you, but I have my work on the environmental monitoring program, and you've got your duties to the Responders.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: People are counting on us to be selfless. To put their needs ahead of ours.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I know, but part of rebuilding the world is... well, having families again, and I think that's an important responsibility, too.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Besides, why even bother trying to survive if there aren't things worth living for?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Look... if this is too soon for you, then I'll wait until you're ready. Just promise you'll tell me if you change your mind.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Okay. I promise.

items.name: The Christmas Flood
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: This is Maria Chavez speaking, and today is December 25th, 2092.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Once, in the world before the war, this would have been a joyous time to celebrate with loved ones. Now it's a time to reflect and to mourn.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: It was on this day ten years ago that we lost so much in the tragic event we call the Christmas Flood.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I'm making this recording in the hopes of ensuring the flood and its victims are never forgotten.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I suppose the story really begins in November of 2077, the month after the war.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Survivors from the Pleasant Valley Ski Resort sent a group to Charleston to ask for help and supplies. The city leaders turned them away.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: There was so much chaos and so much need back then, I suppose it was an impossible request to grant.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: The failure to secure help led to a change in leadership for the survivors at the ski resort.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: A cold and brutal man named David Thorpe took charge, and he shaped those people into something terrible.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: They took what they wanted by force and killed anyone that stood in their way.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Years later, Thorpe's girlfriend Rosalynn led a raid on Charleston. They were spotted early, and a fight broke out.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: A few of them escaped, but Rosalynn was injured and taken prisoner along with some of the other raiders.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: By then, the Responders were more or less running things in the city, and we were doing pretty well for ourselves.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We felt confident we could confront the raiders on their home turf, so we sent a group up into the mountains to see if we could make a deal.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We hoped we could get them to leave us alone if we agreed to release some of the prisoners. We were wrong.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Thorpe had somehow got his hands on a mini-nuke, and he used it to blow the Summersville Dam on Christmas morning.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We lost almost everything; our homes, our supplies and most of our friends and family.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: The days and weeks that followed were the hardest of my life, but somehow, we held together.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We kept the idea of the Responders alive, even though there were only a handful of us left.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: That's the story of the Christmas Flood. Tell your children, tell everyone you meet. Let's keep the memory alive for as long as we can.

items.name: The Fire Breathers
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: All right. We're recording.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Good, 'cause now we can get on record that I think this idea's god-damned looney.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I'm not thrilled about sending our people into a place that's actively toxic either...

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: ... but there are whole towns down there we still haven't reached out to: Welch, Beckley, Bramwell.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Bramwell? Come on, now! You really think the Hornwrights or the Garrahans didn't fly off to some private island the moment the air raid sirens turned on?

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Most likely they did. But right now we don't know and don't have a safe way of finding out.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: And that's why I wanted your help, Melody, on how we can get there.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: ... fine. We got a couple folks from the Charleston Fire Department.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: I can talk to them, see what they have to say about gettin' set up for those sorts of operations.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Anyone you send into all that smoke is going to need training, though. Need to be whip smart if they're gonna survive someplace that hostile.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: And breathing equipment's finicky as hell. Whole lot of care and maintenance if they're gonna be out there for hours, let alone days.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: You're talking about a whole new division here.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I understand what I'm asking.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Tell you what you ought to do... you ought to give 'em a name.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: A name?

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Green Berets. Smokejumpers. Navy Seals. You want someone to sign up for dangerous duty, needs to be some prestige behind it.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: You give 'em a name, a new designation, extra rations, maybe, I'll guarantee you'll get the volunteers you're looking for.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Hmm. Any suggestions?

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Huh... well, gramps was a moonshiner. Made hooch so strong, normal folk couldn't come within a quarter-mile of it.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Everyone called him and his boys the "Fire Breathers." Resilient sons-a-guns. What about that?

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: ... I suppose we don't need to go with the first idea we come up with. But for now, I'd like you to reach out to those firemen.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Convince them to get onboard with the... Fire Breathers. Let them know it's important. Prestigious.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Oh lordy, I think she likes it.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I'll work on getting them a place to train. Charleston Fire Department seems like the natural spot.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Certainly won't have to travel far to get yourselves into trouble.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Good. We should get started. If there's anyone still alive down there, I think they've suffered enough.

location.text: Found at WV Lumber Co. Office.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Say it again so the mic can here you. The name.

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: C-crane.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: And where is this Crane?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: I saw him... we were at this bar. The Wayward. Just north of Flatwoods.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: And what does he know?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: He said he was on the trail of this vault.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: The people kind or the riches kind?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: The kind that holds stuff.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: The kind that holds stuff. I'll consider the topic clarified. You think it's the treasure?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: I don't know. He-he didn't say.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Well, seems like that'd be worth finding out, wouldn't it?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Y-yes?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Are you afraid of me?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Oh god yes.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Don't be. We're not monsters here. We're pragmatists. You can get off the floor.

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Are you--you're not going to kill me?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Not unless you give me a reason. Do you have a place to go?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: N-no.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Do you want one?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: ... w-what would you need me to do?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Go upstairs. Have a meal and a drink, share what you know. Maybe it'll jog some memories. From there... we can talk.

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: And if I wanted to leave?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: We're all free men and women here. A little family. We take care of our own, rest of the world... be damned.

items.name: Too Much Noise
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I talked to Sheila yesterday about finding some food. She said she'd give me the info about a place if I grabbed some for both of us.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I agreed, and she pointed me to an old building nearby filled with machines that could make something she called "cream."

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I never heard of it, but she promised that it tasted good and it would keep us both from starving.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: According to her instructions, all I had to do was push a button and the machines would start cranking out bottles.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: What she forgot to tell me was that it would be loud as hell and attract every creature in earshot.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: It took everything I had to fight the things that swarmed the building. I barely made it out of there alive.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: If anyone finds this, tell Sheila that I'm keeping all of the damn bottles of cream. Next time, she can come get her own.

items.name: Vault Reactor Incident

transcript.speaker: Head Engineer Brass
transcript.text: Don't worry Kelemen! We're getting you out of there!

transcript.speaker: Doctor Loris
transcript.text: Are you insane? The entire reactor is flooded with radiation. We need to quarantine this whole area.

transcript.speaker: Head Engineer Brass
transcript.text: We're not leaving him in there!

transcript.speaker: Doctor Loris
transcript.text: It's not about him anymore. He's already dead. Anyone we send to help is just going to die with him.

transcript.speaker: Head Engineer Brass
transcript.text: You don't know that!

transcript.speaker: Doctor Loris
transcript.text: You're emotional. Not thinking rationally. Medical is locking this area down. That's all there is to it.

items.name: Volunteer Training Program: Food

location.text: Found near Morgantown Airport, near Flatwoods.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Interview two. Reverend Delbert Winters! Hi! I met you in the woods near the Morgantown Airport. You were picking flowers. Why?

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I was harvesting a lot of stuff, actually. I hunted a deer recently. It looked... strange. But tasted fine.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: What's a basic, easy meal that someone who's been surviving on cans could make?

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: You can make tea with dried flowers. It's not much, but it can soothe your stomach.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I don't know what this flower is called, but I call it a Soot Flower. If you add it to water, you can make a tea.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: Same with rabbit meat or chicken meat, you can easily make soups with boiled water.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: God willing, we can adapt old recipes to new types of food.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: What do you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: Back in the army, we got sent off to places with weird fish I never heard of, and weird veggies I'll never see again. You know?

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: We had to cook with 'em still. Just pretend it's catfish or something and see how it turns out.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: But now, well, lemme say that I've seen some weird stuff.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I thought maybe it was unholy, but... these are all the creation of our lord even if man has manipulated them, and dang it, they're still edible.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Oh, um, well. What kind of veggies do you eat?

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: Yeah there are still some edible veggies out there, like melons and carrots and gourds.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: You know, I found some tomatoes and potatoes growing together. They're somehow pollinating each other or something.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I ate one and it was kind of like ketchup-flavored cardboard, but hey, I'm alive.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: You might have to experiment like that. Don't be too picky if it keeps you alive to see the end of times.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Sounds like you've been thinking about this for a while.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: You could say that.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I knew the end was coming for a good long while, and well, it's here... and the end will come again.

transcript.speaker: Delbert Winters
transcript.text: I have faith that there's a reason for all this, and that we need to survive to see our Lord again. And well, we need food to survive.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Fair enough. Thanks for the tips, Delbert.

items.name: Volunteer Training Program: Water
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: This is my first interview with another survivor, Kesha McDermott.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: She found me trying to break into a Nuka-Cola machine and showed me a different way.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: So Kesha... can you tell us a bit about how we can make sure our water is safe for drinking? Try to keep it to the basics for training purposes.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: It's not complicated, really. Find water and strain out any big particles and chunks.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Then boil it in a pot over an open fire for a minute or two, then let it cool. Should be fine. Like making tea, right?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: You joined the Responders a while ago and helped develop a program to train volunteers. So, were you a survivalist prior to all of this?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: You could say that. I taught high school kids!

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: I used to talk about this very thing to them - practical application of the sciences.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: It's fascinating, but... you never realize how important some things will be down the road, do you?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: I guess not. So, if we were students of yours, what would you tell us about the world now? How can we survive?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: That's a good question, Dassa. I would tell you all first of all, to remain calm and focus on surviving.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: The first thing you need to do is get yourself some clean drinking water. It's likely all you'll find is dirty water, but that's ok! We can fix it.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Dirty water carries a small chance of disease and is a bit radioactive. You'll probably survive if you drink it, but you shouldn't take that risk.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: It's better than toxic water or nuclear waste though, which are both very harmful and should be boiled thoroughly first. Got that, Dassa?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Yes'm - contaminated waters should be boiled. Ok. That sounds easy enough. So boiled water is safe?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: It's mostly safe, but still a bit radioactive. What you really want is purified water.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Ohh, purified water. How do I get that?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: You can build machines that will do it for you, and that's the most reliable way. Building them requires some space and time, and plenty of materials.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: But on my way up here from Watoga, I found purified water occasionally in supply caches and medical kits. So keep your eyes peeled.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: If I boil water and that's mostly safe - aside from a teensy bit of radiation - what about tea? Most folks around here are tea drinkers, as you know.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: I recall many a night sipping tea on the stoop, watching lightning bugs and reading a book in peace and quiet. Tell me that's still ok, Kesha?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Oh, bless your heart. It's probably as good as boiled water, anyway! Maybe even better if you add anything medicinal to it.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Some survivors add all sorts of flowers and herbs to boiled water, and they swear by it. Personally, I stick with purified water. To each their own!

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Switching tracks a bit, I know you're awfully busy with your latest research in Flatwoods. Can you explain that a bit?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Of course! I'm testing local, natural water over time in Appalachia. Gathering data, monitoring the radiation and contamination levels, all of that.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: I analyze the data in my lab to look for long term trends, and use those trends to determine how we can use the water right now.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: We use the water for more than just drinking, you know. It feeds our plants which feed our animals... so we need to know how things are changing.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: You've got a lot of work cut out for you. I'm glad you joined the Responders -- that data sounds invaluable!

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: It is. I've integrated the data collection and research into the Responder Survivors Volunteer Program as well. I am still a teacher, after all.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: If anyone wants to help, just become a volunteer in Flatwoods and get a water testing kit from me. It's a fast process but it helps a lot.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Dip the test strips in the river and in the water pump's water and analyze the test strips at my terminal in the lab. That's all. Easy, right?

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Help me with this research and you'll help everybody live a little safer. And you can see how our environment has changed first hand - with science!

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Wow, and there you have it, folks. Thanks for talking with us today, Kesha. And thanks for showing us all how to live a little safer.

transcript.speaker: Kesha McDermott
transcript.text: Mhmm. Class dismissed!

items.name: Volunteer Training: Camping 101
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Responder Survivors Volunteer Program: Advanced Training: Camping. By Miguel Caldera -- robot programmer extraordinaire!

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Part 1: Finding the perfect camping location.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Now that the world has changed, it's hard to stay safe. Used to be that camping was safe as houses. *laughs* Well, until there was a strong wind.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: These days, nothing is really safe. Even in your camp, someone might hurt you. The perfect spot doesn't matter now. It's all about your defenses!

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: You can build near people you trust who will watch your back, or build things that will watch your back for you! No problem! Anyone can do it.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Remember, camps are mobile. We're all explorers now, camping in a strange land full of adventure, wonder, and danger. So camp often, and rest a lot.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Before the war, I was going to retire and go camping. Now I can do it every day, forever! It's a dream come true! Do what you love, right?

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Now come to my camp and I can show you some knots and framing techniques. Then I'll direct you on to some helpful supplies! Good luck, Volunteer!

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: Guys, do you feel this? Do you feel this, guys? Guys? Huh, where did everybody... AAAAAH, WHAT THE HELL IS THAT??

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: OOOH MAN, please tell me you see that? Guys, do you see that? Becky, there's a lighthouse there, right? Right Becky? Steve? Oh god! OH GOD!

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict

transcript.speaker: Earle Williams
transcript.text: Hey Mags... listen, I know I messed up. I never should have came into this mine in the first place... a few supplies ain't worth all this.

transcript.speaker: Earle Williams
transcript.text: Don't you for one second start thinking that I left you on purpose, and don't be going and blaming yourself either.

transcript.speaker: Earle Williams
transcript.text: I can't be there for you anymore, but you're tough and I know you'll be okay... Never forget your pops loves you more than anything.

items.name: A Night at the Neapolitan, Part 1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: It takes a lot of chems to get thrown out of the Neapolitan, but we were riding the line.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: My confidant and I made the trip to cover the Showmen's Games, a world renowned exercise in high stakes barbarism. Few in the entertainment world could match.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: Instead, we spent most of our time getting hopped up on Daddy-O and chugging bourbon in the casino bar.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: It seemed the logical course of action. The Games were notoriously deadly, even for bystanders.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: Liquid courage and a head full of hallucinogens were the obvious defense.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: What we didn't count on was the Devil's Blood. We had never heard of the stuff, and for good reason - it's an AC specialty.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: We weren't supposed to have it. It wasn't meant for us, but for the real high rollers.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: The people who, even in a world ravaged by pestilence and war, still managed to come out on top. But we found a way.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: The exclusivity made it all the sweeter. Not because we aspired to that lifestyle - quite the opposite.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: We wanted to soil the royal concoction inside our mangy, flea-ridden hides.

items.name: A Night at the Neapolitan, Part 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: One hit is all it took to realize we'd made a terrible mistake. Even for degenerates as celebrated as ourselves, this was too much.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: The trip wasn't bad, it was glorious - horrifyingly so. We knew, instantly, that this was what money could buy. And we knew we'd never have it again.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: We witnessed firsthand the life that was being kept from us, and as much as we wanted to reach out and take it...

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: ...we couldn't do anything more than slump in our chairs and watch as it drifted away.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: The consequences would be more than spiritual. Every inch of our bodies yearned for more after that first hit.

transcript.speaker: Jack Hunter
transcript.text: Addictol won't be enough to cure this hunger. Maybe nothing will.

items.name: Anthropologist's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: As my study of Hopewell Cave continues, I'm struck by the atypical nature of this Adena-based burial complex.

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: The Adena culture generally buried their dead in large mounds and similar hill-shaped earthworks.

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: Due to the primitive nature of the tools from 1000 to 200 BC, stone carving was not yet a part of their society.

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: However, archeologists who investigated this "skull cave" site removed remains and artifacts belonging to the Adena culture.

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: I wonder if it's possible that the remains of the Adena people were moved to this location well after their society ceased to exist?

transcript.speaker: Anthropologist
transcript.text: For one culture to treat another's with such reverence is unusual at best. I will continue my research to discover more.

items.name: ATLAS Research Log #104
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: ATLAS Project, Research Log, #104.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: Lieutenant Marcs and I have begun calibrating the ion beam accelerator.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: We've hit a plateau at the 300 MeV threshold. Micro-variations in the magnetic flux are disrupting the Betatron induction loop.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: The Lieutenant is working on a firmware update for the coil controller. She said she'll have the 'wobble' out by Monday.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: Assembly of the main device remains on schedule. The Air Force is nothing if not punctual.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: Colonel Oberlin is still pressing for the facility to be fully operational before the end of the year.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: As much as I want to see my research in action, we need to proceed carefully. If this goes wrong, the results could be catastrophic.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: ATLAS has the potential to change the world. Or destroy it.

items.name: ATLAS Research Log #293
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: ATLAS Project, Research Log 292. 93? 93.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: It's been five months. Five months since that day.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: They abandoned me. The military never believed in ATLAS. It was just another weapon. When the nukes fell, what did it matter?

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: ATLAS, this research... it's been my life's work. We need ATLAS. The world needs ATLAS. Now more than ever.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: I have to finish it. Everything I need, it's all here. I just need time. And hands.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: I've activated all of the robots. They're security bots, they were never programmed for this. But it's all I've got. I can make it work.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: I've replaced the main lens. Finished the particle analysis. I think the accelerator is finally stable.

transcript.speaker: Isaac Hammond
transcript.text: I'm so tired. But I have to keep going. Just a little more. It's almost done. Almost done.

items.name: Blackwater Mine: Innovations
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: This is Foreman Hibbs. United States Department of Energy.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: Blackwater Mine has changed a lot over the years. Plenty of you already know what happens when a mine tunnel hits groundwater, so the pumps shouldn't be too surprising.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: But yeah, just to put any rumors to bed, we're also trying some new ways of getting at those precious rocks.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: And yes, it involves melting the Uranium while it's still underground and siphoning it up. Sure beats hauling it by hand, if it works.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: Now don't think that means any of you are getting extra time-off. Stop listening to this and get back to work.

items.name: Blackwater Mine: Orientation
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: This is Foreman Hibbs. United States Department of Energy.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: If you're hearing this, then, welcome aboard and all that.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: I'm sure the Human Resources folks have gotten you situated, but there's one thing I need to make sure we've drilled into ya, so you're gonna get it again.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: Blackwater Mine is a government Uranium site. That means you're a federal employee, now.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: And all those background checks and security interviews you went through wasn't just for fun.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: Every yield we fail to bring up is a national security problem. One less missile gets made. One less power plant gets fuel.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: Department of Energy isn't messing around. I'm not messing around.

transcript.speaker: Foreman Hibbs
transcript.text: So stop listening to this and get back to work. Let's dig up some shiny rocks and hope they don't make us sterile.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Tannin! Another scotch.

transcript.speaker: Protectron
transcript.text: Ma'am.

transcript.speaker: Dorothy Orris
transcript.text: What about you, Liz? Have you made up your mind yet?

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth White
transcript.text: Oh, Bill's keen on Charleston. We were social with the Governor. I'm sure he'd make arrangements for us.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Hollingsworth
transcript.text: Evans? That snake?

transcript.speaker: Dorothy Orris
transcript.text: He always was for sale. Not a terrible thing, if you're the buyer.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Can you imagine, parading into town like a troupe of beggars?

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: And Charleston, no less! It always was a slum. Now? With refugees swarming like flies? Ugh.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: No, the resorts are the better option. If The Whitespring won't have us, we should try Pleasant Valley. Even Sunnytop.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth White
transcript.text: Sunnytop? Really?

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: I'm not there for the skiing. Or the clientele.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: But I'd rather stay at a shoddy lodge than take my chances with... whatever might be going on down in the valley.

transcript.speaker: Protectron
transcript.text: Ma'am.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Chapter 7: Constructing the Effigy

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Gather ten to twenty bundles of sticks underneath a new moon.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Bind them tightly with the entrails of the sacrificial beast, and cleanse and bless your tools with holy incense.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Construct the form of your effigy with the bundles, using straw or twine to fix them into position.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Plant a staff of hewn oak down the center of the effigy.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Hammer the staff firmly into the dirt, and pile more sticks, logs, and wood scraps around the base.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Anoint your sacred blade with the holy oil made from the Bright One's eggs, and use your blade to bless the effigy for use in your circle.

transcript.text: Chapter 8: Summoning Rite

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: On the night of a full moon, gather your fellows and sit around the effigy.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Light the pyre, and have all recite the following incantation as one:

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: O Bright One, we bid thee. Follow this sacred flame with thy ever watchful eyes.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: See clear as day this holy fire we burn in your honor. Like cattle to slaughter, we die for thee.

transcript.speaker: Cultist
transcript.text: Bid us welcome as we beckon thee with this Divine Lamp, that we may be blessed by the air underneath thy wings.

items.name: Concerns With Margie
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: Meg here. I've gotta say something before it's too late. I think ol' Margie's off her rocker, man.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: You know, we're all tryin' our best here, but this whole idea of being a Raider without killing is way harder than it sounds.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: I mean, yeah, I get it, but, damn girl! This is life and death out there!

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: Some of these people are just tryin' to make it, like anyone else after the bombs. I don't want to kill 'em if they don't give up their stuff.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: But you know, we got to eat, and so do they. Wavin' a gun around used to scare 'em, but now they got nothin' to lose, so they wave one right back.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: I keep tellin' Margie we're losin' people out there because we're told not to fire first, and it ain't getting' any easier.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: She don't know it yet, but a lot of us've been firin' first anyway, so's to save our skins.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: Margie'd be pissed, but she ain't out there like the rest of us. So, to heck with her.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: Only reason we don't up and mutiny her ass is because she's got that piece of the key for the cache, and a few loyalists to protect her.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: And honestly, it still beats hangin' with any of the other gangs. That deal we've got with the Palace is pretty sweet. All told, we got it good.

transcript.speaker: Meg Groberg
transcript.text: Ah well. Guess all we can do is keep on keepin' on, ya dig?

items.name: Cryptid Sighting: Grafton Monster 9/27
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Beverly Solomon, Cryptid Analyst, 9/27/77. Grafton Monster witness report.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: This is from one of those spelunkers that roam the hills looking for abandoned mining claims. Can you imagine?

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Well, the classic four-foot wide shoulders, headless profile, deep sonorous cry, they got a good glance at it. The witness didn't know what it was, but the description is very clear.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: It came out when she started playing a mouth harp, apparently! I'm going to go out to go look. Maybe that sound is the key....

items.name: Cryptid Sighting: Snallygaster 10/4
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Beverly Solomon, Cryptid Analyst, 10/4/77. Snallygaster witness report.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Another interesting tidbit from the locals, this time about the Snallygaster. This one's for you, Teddy!

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Alright, so the witness overheard a loud shrieking sound and was rushed by a dark shape in the woods. It was leaping at them, or maybe flying?

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: They took shelter in an old german settler's barn and it couldn't get at them, which is what really interested me!

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: It screamed and hollered outside all night until dawn, but they knew the seven-pointed star on the wall outside would keep them safe.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Yikes, I guess I know what my next tattoo is gonna be!

items.name: Cryptid Sighting: Wendigo 10/25
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Beverly Solomon, Cryptid Analyst, 10/25/77. Wendigo witness report.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Ooh, this is a spooky tale! Okay, so this is my own personal sighting.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: I was up at the ski lodge this past week, enjoying some well-deserved R&R.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: I guess I can never really be off the clock though, because I happened to see something hunched on the slopes ahead of me.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: I thought it was some old coat, you know? I was moving pretty fast, so I was just trying to avoid it.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: Anyhow, it just unfurls as I get close. Must've been ten feet tall, but just all skin and bones like a dead dog.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: It had a deer's skull cracked open in its hands from the fresh kill it was eating, and as I go by I get this powerful cold feeling through my bones.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: I thought to myself, you know ... Bev, you really lucked out getting that tattoo before coming out here on this trip.

transcript.speaker: Beverly Solomon
transcript.text: I can't imagine what kind of things I'm gonna see next!

location.text: Found near Palace of the Winding Path.

routes.name: near Palace of the Winding Path

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Warm greetings, friend!

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, warm greetings, and wholeness, and all that... You, uh, wanted to see me?

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Yes, indeed I did, Disciple Simon.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: I'm proud of everything you've accomplished here in such a short time, but I'm having concerns about our "new direction."

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: You mean the uh, "Transitory Disciple Program?" What's the problem? Are the guests complaining?

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Quite the opposite. By the time they depart, they appear blissful and enlightened. It's wonderful!

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: No, it's a far more material issue, I'm afraid. The amount of money that you're spending to advertise the Palace has me concerned.

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: Don't let those sorts of matters worry you, Cyrus. After all, that's why you appointed me as the Palace's business manager.

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: You just go and get naked and run around lighting incense, painting watermelons, or whatever you need to do. Leave the rest to me.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Come now, Disciple Simon. You're beginning to sound similar to when you first arrived at our doorstep.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Oh my, perhaps your balance has shifted. Did you wish to be anointed in oils for a cleansing?

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: No, no. I'm fine, quite balanced. Everything is great. No more anointing please.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: Very well. Perhaps I'm worrying needlessly.

transcript.speaker: Cyrus
transcript.text: After all, it is you who has gifted us with this new direction and brought so many people here to achieve wholeness.

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: Yeah, no sweat there Cyrus. Don't even worry about it.

transcript.speaker: Simon Gladwell
transcript.text: Anyway, uh, since I'm here, I need you to look at these plans for a ventilatio..., uh, I mean " for Spiritual Conduits," I want to have installed.

items.name: Everything Changes
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: It's funny what comes to mind at a time like this.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: When I was little, I used to come here with my grandfather.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Every morning, we'd sit right here, have donuts, read the paper. Just the two of us.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Everything changes. They got rid of the donuts. And the staff. And the whole world.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: But this spot... it's still here.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Joyce did her best. They all did. I hope they make it out there.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: As for me? I'm going to stay right here. Have one last donut. And whatever happens, happens.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Everything changes. But in the end? I can't imagine a place I'd rather be.

items.name: FEV Research Log #1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number One.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Under any other circumstance, it would feel foolish to begin recording these before my work has even meaningfully begun.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I developed this habit during my graduate studies. A tool, helping me as much to retain insights as to preserve my failures.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Here, when nothing about what I am to undertake is normal, I break with tradition and start these logs now. Posterity requires this moment be kept.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: What I am about to do will almost assuredly make of me a villain in the eyes of many. My work is distasteful, and must be conducted in secret.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Here, for whatever person may one day hear this, I say for the record that what I will do I do out of love. An unselfish love that knows no rest.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Not for a person. No clichéd deceased spouse or lost child motivates me. Humanity is my love, though none would accuse me of excess sentiment.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: We are a species tormented by the ravages of the Great War, reduced to vermin eking out an existence in the rubble of the world that was.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The mistakes of my past are writ on the face of every survivor living in fear of the mutated horrors that stalk the Wasteland.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I can correct this. I must. We are not meant to live like this. There is a way forward, to free us from the horrors we...I...created.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Yet, I fear the failures that lie between me and the future I see. They will be many, and they will cause a great deal of pain before I am done.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The sins of West Tek must be undone. The price will be extreme, but it must be paid. If my life is included in that price, I will pay it gladly.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I record this log not to seek forgiveness. I neither deserve nor require it.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I ask only that you, my hypothetical listener, know that the things to come are not the product of ill-intent or a sadistic mania.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: One day, good will come of the evil I am set to do. I hope that you are there to see it, and understand.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #112
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number One Hundred and Twelve.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: My work's demand for human subjects has increased dramatically as I make ground toward my ultimate goal.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: To this end, I have contracted with a group of mercenaries calling themselves the Hellcat Company. Trustworthy, if such a term applies here.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: They display a useful moral flexibility. They do not question the nature of my work or my need for human subjects, and I do not illuminate them.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Already they have begun acquiring new subjects at far greater pace than I could, and a contingent remain to guard the Vault itself.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I must be careful. A mercenary is only as loyal as their pay, after all. My control of the Vault security systems keeps them in check for now.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #13
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Thirteen.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Whatever the prior occupants of this Vault may have done, I must thank them, especially Chief Engineer Doctor Memling.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The good doctor, while a respectable scientist in his own right, had the classic engineer's idiosyncratic approach to maintenance.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: His additions to the Vault reactor and electrical subsystems provide me with ample points of connection to directly access mains power.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Between this and certain defects in reactor shielding, I have invaluable resources for my research.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: My first attempts in this area are more disappointing, however. Lacking Memling's expertise, my electrical impedance tests failed dramatically.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The unintentional discovery of a new method of rapidly cooking a mole rat fails even in that regard:

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Molerat exposed to several thousand volts at significant amperage does not make for an appetizing sight.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Nonetheless, these results are duly recorded and I believe my understanding of the system is sufficient to produce more useful results in the future.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #148
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number One Hundred and Forty-Eight.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I can feel the end approaching. The equations fall into place, and I can see the shape of it, the perfected FEV, even in my restless dreams.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: That vision of the goal is the only succor now. What I have done to reach it can never be washed away. I have been right, but that is small comfort.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I give them numbers now, and try not to listen when they speak to me, pleading. I prefer to sedate them when removing them from their holding cells

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Unconscious, they cannot weep, or stare accusingly at me. I cannot make them understand that we are alike part of a greater destiny.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: They think me inhuman, uncaring. I know I would be no different, were our roles reversed. I do not blame them for hating me.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I lie in my cot at night and see their faces. I remember them all, and wait for sleep to carry me to the visions of when I can finally stop.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Final candidate number three is ready for verification. I am within two, perhaps three iterations of success.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Will I be able to sleep untroubled when this is over? Or will punishment for what I have done be a mercy, freeing me from its memory?

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #17
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Seventeen.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I am no longer alone in this endeavor. Against all odds, I have made contact with a former colleague, Doctor Farha, whom fate preserved as it did me.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Doctor Farha was reluctant when I first described my aims. The testing that will be required, and the failures, give her pause.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Even at university, we clashed on the ethical boundaries of research. Regardless, I have convinced her to aid me despite her doubts.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I will continue to work here in Vault 96, in secrecy. Doctor Farha, meanwhile has established a laboratory suitable for mass-production.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: She has acquired a foundling of sorts, a young woman by the name of Nellie Wright. She seems something of a prodigy.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I believe it was Ms. Wright's enthusiastic support of my ideas that convinced Doctor Farha to acquiesce to my request for aid.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Farha has also brought in Jain. I knew him from university, and our time at West Tek. This work is his chance at redemption as much as my own.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #22
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Twenty-Two.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: In retrospect, my enthusiasm for the cryogenically-preserved specimens in the Vault was excessive, if not actually misplaced.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I am down to the last four viable test subjects. Further research is at an impasse unless I move to human subjects.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Obtaining volunteers will be impossible. The necessary experimentation to even approach a functional result will be unavoidably fatal to some.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I will have to take extreme measures to obtain subjects. Thousands, perhaps millions of lives will be saved. Utility trumps sentimentality.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #38
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Thirty-Eight.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The capture of human test subjects is itself less difficult than I imagined.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The people of Appalachia are in bad need of medicine, and lone travelers are easy to approach when one is a doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I tell myself these acts are necessary - the work too important, and I cannot complete it without living human subjects to experiment upon.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Yet as I compound failure upon failure, in my quiet hours I question what I have made of myself in pursuit of this goal.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I began this enterprise fully cognizant of what it might take, but even with that foreknowledge I could not comprehend the weight of it.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Have I become no different from that fool Elias, a font of monsters with no humane end in sight? Am I deluded in believing myself capable of success?

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: These moments pass. I push aside those doubts and focus on the work before me. The people of Appalachia need this. The world needs this.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Let them vilify me when they learn what I have done. I will make a better future for them, even if I do not live to see it myself.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #5
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Five.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The creators of the Forced Evolutionary Virus were idiot savants. They saw weapons, soldiers to win a war that would end almost as soon as it began.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: They had discovered a means by which we could seize the reigns of human evolution, and all they could envision was more efficient death.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: My colleagues at West Tek were likewise fools. They made the virus a plaything and Huntersville their ant farm, shaking it to watch them scurry.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The FEV was never meant to create abominations. At its core is something wondrous and hopeful. I will free it from what they made of it.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Humanity will have the future it should have had, and a better human will build that world, free from fear.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: FEV Research Log #57
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Research Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Number Fifty-Seven.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I begin to doubt my own sanity at times. My efforts, while not without progress, continue to fail to bear real fruit.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The FEV seems almost deliberately malignant, as if it had a consciousness and rejects my every attempt to bend it toward a benevolent end.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I have come to recognize the signs of imminent metastasis and conversion to the so-called "Super Mutant" state.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I am ill-equipped to deal with the product of such failure, and have taken to disposing of these unfortunates outside the Vault itself.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I regret that my current methods of disposal may, in the short term, increase the Super Mutant population in Appalachia, but it cannot be avoided.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: First days in Vault 79
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: AC
transcript.text: Just finished offloading before the Big Drop. Even here in the vault we can hear the nukes going off.

transcript.speaker: AC
transcript.text: Command says it should be safe to go top side in six to twelve months.

transcript.speaker: AC
transcript.text: Meanwhile, we'll start shuffling gold bars into the operations shaft.

transcript.speaker: AC
transcript.text: Even if we can go top side shortly, you can bet the former depository is just a slag heap.

transcript.speaker: AC
transcript.text: The gold is probably going to stay here for a long time.

items.name: Freddie Lang's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: So I, uh, found this old holotape to record onto... Look, I know this is stupid. You can't hear me, not anymore. I dunno. Maybe this is more for me.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: I just... miss you, Lucie, more than you could ever imagine. And, I can't help but feel responsible somehow.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: They were firing up the snowmakers, and I knew you didn't like skiing, so I didn't even mention I was going. I thought you'd talk me out of it.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: I wish I had told you, though. We're both hard-headed, but one of our stubborn asses would have caved and then we'd be together, one way or another.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: Maybe it's for the best. These... people I'm with probably wouldn't understand us either. I've had to get even tougher than before.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: I've had to steal, and kill, and worse still, I've had to hide who I am behind this facade. I'm alive...I guess? But who am I now?

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: Am I still the same Alfreda you knew? Would you even still like me? I'd hope you would understand.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: Gotta be strong to survive, and if that means playing mean and leading a bunch of other monsters to prey on the weak, then that's what I gotta do.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: <distant muffled shouting and commotion>

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: Sounds like the boys are getting back. I'd better go. Put that mean face back on.

transcript.speaker: Freddie Lang
transcript.text: I wish the bombs never took you from me, Lucie. I love you. Always will.

items.name: Geraldine Fitzsimmon's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: It's been barely a week since the bombs fell, and supplies have become scarce.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: The former guests at the resort are exploring the feasibility of sending out scavenging groups to hunt down whatever they can find.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: What's starting to dawn on us is that there will be people outside the resort sending groups of their own.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: Who knows if they'll be friendly, or simply take what they want?

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: Instead of waiting to find out, we've concluded that our goods should be locked up for safe keeping.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: It's a smart move and one that will keep our belongings protected until the government rescue teams arrive.

transcript.speaker: Geraldine Fitzsimmons
transcript.text: It's good to know that there's still some rationality left amidst all this chaos.

items.name: Harland's Up To No Good

location.text: Found near Pleasant Valley Ski Resort.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Rosalynn Jeffries
transcript.text: They're talkin' crap about you again, David. This time I'm gonna record them so you can hear it yourself.

transcript.speaker: Rosalynn Jeffries
transcript.text: <Quiet movement>

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: I know, Harland, I know. But what are we going to do? David's... not a very reasonable man.

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: You saw what he did, Margie! He killed those innocent people who came to help us. He killed them in cold blood! And for what? A few measly supplies?

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: The man's defied you at every turn. He does what he wants. The people chose you to lead them, not that blowhard!

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: Lower your voice, Harland. You don't need to yell at me.

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: I'm sorry, dear. You're right. I just... I don't know what to do anymore. I don't want to live like this, like some sort of...

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: Like some sort of savages? I know, don't worry. We'll deal with it. I'll hold a trial with the aim to exile him for his crimes.

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: And if he chooses not to participate in this trial, what then? You're aware more and more people are starting to side with him, right?

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: Not everyone is willing to follow a foolish madman. Trust me, Harland. Reason will win out in the end.

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: I'll tell you. I'm inclined to go over there and give him a piece of my mind.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: Now Harland, dear, don't do anything stupid...

transcript.speaker: Harland McClintock
transcript.text: Oh you know me, I'm just upset is all. It might just be pissin' into the wind, but I'm still going to talk with him. I'll be civil. Promise.

items.name: Holden McMerrick's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: Ever since the bombs dropped, the former guests at the ski resort have lost their minds.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: If being a member of the Honorary Mock-Naval Yachting Society has taught me one thing, it's that preparation is the key to survival.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: The idiots here have locked up their belongings and split up the access key, stashing away valuable items we could be using for barter.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: Every decision being made is foolish!

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: Instead of using this facility as a headquarters and sending out hunting parties to look for scraps, we need to find a new base of operations.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: We should band together in larger groups and take anything we find along the way.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: They're convinced the government is going to rescue us, but the truth of the matter is that we're on our own.

transcript.speaker: Holden McMerrick
transcript.text: The only people that can help us now are ourselves.

items.name: Hornwright's Proposal
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: I'd like to thank the Monongah Township Council for letting me attend your meeting today.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: For those of you that don't know me, I'm Daniel Hornwright, CEO of Hornwright Industrial.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: I'm here with an offer...

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: No, strike that. I'm here with a proposal so beneficial and so incredibly lucrative, that simply calling it an "offer" doesn't begin to do it justice.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: I want to purchase the mining rights to Monongah Mine from your town. Not only for a generous sum of cash up front, but for perpetual...

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: ...that means forever... royalties for every single ton of coal that we extract.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: What do you have to provide in return? Nothing. How much money does the town have to outlay initially? Not a penny.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: All I need is for you to sign on this dotted line, and sit back while the money rolls in.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Hornwright
transcript.text: No risk, all reward. And most important, no chance that anyone from this town ever gets hurt in that mine again. I humbly await your reply.

items.name: Huntersville Memories
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Personal Log, Doctor Edgar Blackburn. Huntersville.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: I should never have allowed Dumont to convince me to stay with West Tek when they shuttered the Greenhouse Initiative.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The Pan-Immunity Virion was intended to shield us from biological warfare and make the population safe from the horrors war could unleash.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The Greenhouse Initiative turned the same work to feeding the ever-increasing starving masses. Noble goals and worthy science.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: The discovery of the FEV abandoned all that. The awesome potential of the virus, what it could do if harnessed to those same ends - ignored.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Instead they saw a weapon. Super soldiers. Small-minded bureaucrats and their pet scientists had the keys to human evolution and saw profit and war.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Dr. Khan - a disgrace to that title, in the end - took over, and even those miserable goals were cast aside in favor of the perverse.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Infecting the water supply of Huntersville just to observe the effects - why? We knew the virus in its current state produced horrors.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Had we been looking for a cure, perhaps it could have been justified. But Khan had no such interest. He did it because he could.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: Were I a better man, a better scientist, I would have left immediately. My belated resignation does me little credit.

transcript.speaker: Doctor Blackburn
transcript.text: End log.

items.name: Impromptu Raider Meeting
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: Put the gun down, we're here to talk.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: You repping the Cutthroats?

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Maybe. Who's asking?

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: Name's Repo. I'm repping the Diehards.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Frank. So what's this all about?

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: It's about survival. Our gangs are getting picked off one-by-one.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Yeah, by other gangs. That's how things work.

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: The hell with that! We're dying out here. All of Appalachia's trying to kill us, and it's got nothing to do with turf or loot.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: You talking about the Gourmands? Those idiots ate each other to death.

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: Not just the Gourmands, but the Blackwater Bandits, the Trappers - hell, all of us.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Yeah, it's a rough world, I get it. So what's your point?

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: My point is we need to band together. Watch each other's back. If we don't, we might just end up disappearing.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: What's in it for us?

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: Staying alive? Do you understand what I'm saying or you too stupid?

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Don't ever say that again.

transcript.speaker: Repo
transcript.text: This is what I'm talking about. Pointing that gun at me again isn't going to solve anything.

transcript.speaker: Frank
transcript.text: Yeah it will. It'll get you to shut the hell up.
<Single gunshot rings out>

transcript.speaker: Dale
transcript.text: What the hell?! He killed Repo! Shoot him... shoot him!
<Gunfire, multiple shots from different guns>

items.name: Jen's Goodbye
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: I'll make this brief. I'm leaving, and I don't want anyone to come looking for me. I already said my goodbyes to some of you.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: If I didn't say goodbye, it's probably because you're a jerk. Maybe that's shocking to hear, I don't know, I don't really care.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: So uh ... if you run into me in the Capital Wasteland then kindly leave me alone. Thanks in advance, and bye forever!

items.name: Jen's Goodbye
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: Hey asshole, I left this tape here just for you.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: I bet you came here to see if you could get your gold back, didn't you? Well, tough luck.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: You'll never see me again ... but I might be seeing you. Bye now!

items.name: Jen's Journal, Entry 1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: Jen's journal, first entry. If you're not an older, wiser me then you shouldn't be listening to this!

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: Naw, I'm kidding. Paige told me I should consider journaling to help me establish future goals. *laughs* Right? Me, have goals?

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: Anyway, he says it also helps to digest experiences. Maybe that's true, maybe not. I guess we'll find out!

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: A lot has happened lately and I feel so grateful that Foundation-Paige took me in years ago, and that everyone's been so kind and patient.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: We went up against some real challenges and we succeeded. It feels really good, actually.

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: So how's that for digesting my experiences? *burp*

transcript.speaker: Jen
transcript.text: Yikes, that was really pathetic! I'm sorry. I expected ... more of myself. Okay, wait, was that a personal goal?! *laughs* I am killing this!

items.name: Joyce's Message
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Dave? Dave, honey, it's Joyce.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I... I don't know if you'll ever get this. But I wanted to make sure there was something here, if you came looking, if you made it.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: God, where to start?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: It's... it's about two-thirty in the morning. New Year's. 2079.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I've been here for the past year, since the war. Me, a couple of the staff, about a hundred guests. And the robots.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Never thought I'd be grateful for the robots.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: We made out all right. Even made me manager. Can you believe it?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: But... we have to go. Paula and I, we're leaving for Charleston in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I've missed you and the girls. Missed you so, so much. Take care of them for me, all right?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: All my love. Always.

items.name: Knight Connors: Report
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: Starting recording, Knight Alan Connors, Brotherhood of Steel... Aw, one second, lemme toss another one on the fire.
(Wood crackles as a log is tossed on the fire)

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: Ah screw it, I'll do a status report later. This one's... off the record.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: Odessa, Daniel... I'm about half way through the night shift, and it's gotten me thinking.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: I know it's been tough on you two. Neither of you are quite the grizzled old timers that Leila and I are.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: I just want you both to know how proud I am. Not just to see you rise to the challenge, but to see you do it with such vigor and determination.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: For every bit of trouble this trip has been, it's only just started. But I hope you can enjoy calm nights like these... And take a moment to relax.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: Look, each of us have our reasons for being here... including Leila. You may not always see eye to eye, but know that she cares deeply for both of you.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: And Daniel, I know you probably feel she cares too much, but that's just her way.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: Leading from the heart has always worked out for her in the past... And trust me, man, I've been through the thick of it with her.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: In this journey ahead, we're going to need to rely on each other with unwavering support. The toughest trials have yet to come.

transcript.speaker: Knight Connors
transcript.text: But remember: we're more than a Brotherhood now; we're a family.

items.name: Margie McClintock's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: This is Margie McClintock of the Diehards. Heh, what a joke. We deluded ourselves into thinking our victims would fear a name like that.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: But now, everyone out there is as desperate as we are. When every confrontation could mean life or death, people take their chances. They fight back.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: So we have to kill, we have to murder innocent people... Well, not me. I don't care what this world has come to, it's not taking me down with it.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: The whole idea of the Raiders is sick. It's inhuman. I'm destroying that stupid key fragment.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: <Sound of Margie smashing a holotape>

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: Those bastards don't deserve their treasures unless they return to their senses and quit this whole murderous power game they're playing.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: If that ever happens, Vincent knows what to do. Maybe he'll be more successful than I was

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: As for me, I'm leaving. I'll... find some chems, and I'll go out that way, peaceful, without pain... I'm done.

transcript.speaker: Margie McClintock
transcript.text: I'll see you soon, Harland, my love. It's been too long.

items.name: Missile Silo State Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.
